suggestions.edit: New 'interview' persona format: each given answer as 'Interviewer: <question> (options: ...)' then 'Me: <chosen answer>', in the respondent's own voice, keeping the options as the full format does. Instructions unchanged from round 3.
suggestions.answers_result: Every instruction that shifted how often agents buy (rounds 2 and 6) flattened spread; the compact format (round 5) dropped unchosen options and lost pricing group gaps. The persona's form is the untried lever that keeps all the information.
suggestions.why: Out of One, Many conditions on an interviewer-and-me transcript whose answers come from the interviewer's options, and notes its template was never optimised.
suggestions.expected: Right person and group gaps up through closer continuity with the respondent's own voice.
suggestions.risk: Like compact, a format change can move pricing group gaps either way.

suggestions.edit: Add one bullet: 'You are a real person, not a helpful assistant: people often say no, don't care, or hold views others dislike. Don't choose an answer because it sounds agreeable, positive or helpful.'
suggestions.answers_result: Agents say yes to everyday necessities people pass on (milk 1.00 vs 0.50, coffee 0.70 vs 0.25, round 3 tuning set).
suggestions.why: The Anthology paper finds instruction-tuned models conditioned on a backstory give only positive and helpful actions.
suggestions.risk: Rounds 2 and 6 show that shifting agents' overall readiness to buy cuts spread; policy answers, where people support most proposals, could also move the wrong way.

suggestions.edit: Policy only: 'Political opinions: combine all of your background. Party is one part, but your age, religion, income and your own answers about values also shape each view.'
suggestions.answers_result: Agents still put Democrats and Republicans 1.3-2.9 points apart against people's 0.2-1.3; round 1's party fix raised policy right person 0.799 -> 0.826 but not the pooled check.
suggestions.why: Out of One, Many finds party the most predictive element, but no single element carries the prediction and combining them predicts best.
suggestions.expected: Policy right person up; pooled checks likely within noise, since policy is a fifth of the items.
suggestions.risk: Small pooled effect: probably a discard under the keep rule.

method_note.suggestion: Re-measure round 3's kept instructions once on the check set and compare later rounds with the mean of its two runs (trigger 1, waiting for Steven).
method_note.why: Out of One, Many expects variation between draws and no individual-level match; round 3's group gaps of 0.852 sits above every other run (0.765-0.840).
